body.p:
said: the swiftest punishment is that of betrayal and perjury
and of him whom the distraught pleads with or the offender asks to forgive and forget but who
neither pardons nor forgives, though he is able to do so. He fails to observe
the conduct of the righteous who does not do their deeds.

p.n: The Rat Must Fulfill the Pact

body.p:
As I did make haste
to deliver and help you, you, too, should be assiduous in delivering me from
these bonds.’”

“The rat said: ‘A Friend can be one of two kinds: either complaisant
or compelled, yet both seek benefits and are wary of harm. One should
be open toward the complaisant and trust him whatever the situation; as

for the compelled,
there are two situations in which you can be open toward him and others in which you remain cautious of him.

p.n: Friendship Is Pursued For a Need

body.p:
so[, in these situations, the sensible man
always holds back a need of the other for some danger that remains and which he fears; and

p.n: Friendship Is Pursued For a Need

body.p:
on the whole, connections
and mutual love among people only exist to seek an immediate or anticipated benefit.

p.n: The Rat Explains the Reasons for Self-Protection

body.p:
for each action has
a set time,
and whatever is not carried out in its proper time, will have no outcome.

p.n: The Rat Explains Not Cutting the Last Rope

body.p:
I will cut all of your bonds
but will leave one knot to guarantee my safety from you and won't cut it until the time
when I know your attention to be distracted from me and that you cannot reach me when you become freed from the bonds.’”

p.n: The Rat Cuts All but One Rope

body.p: and when morning came, they suddenly saw the huntsman approaching from afar.
